how: Read from Runway's OWN OpenAPI specification, its changelog and its pricing page — NOT PROBED and no request was sent. The aleph2 variant was resolved out of the discriminated oneOf on POST /v1/video_to_video (the model property is a const, not an enum). Re-derive by fetching the spec and selecting the variant whose model const is aleph2.
probe_note: A free probe was deliberately NOT attempted. Marble validates before it starts a world, so its contract could be read from refusals for nothing — but that is a property of a provider, not a law. RBF-001 measured a FAILED Seedance job still charging $1.658. Whether Runway refuses an invalid body without billing is unestablished, and establishing it costs a request that may be charged. The documentation is authoritative enough for an adapter; a probe would only add confidence about error shapes.

fields.name: videoUri
fields.note: The input video to edit. Must be 30 seconds or shorter. HTTPS URL, Runway upload URI, or a base64 data URI capped at 5MB.

fields.name: promptText
fields.note: OPTIONAL — the aggregator presented it as required.

schema.source: Runway OpenAPI spec, /v1/video_to_video, the oneOf variant whose model const is aleph2

duration.note: There is NO duration field on the aleph2 variant. The bound is a property of the SOURCE video — videoUri says "Must be 30 seconds or shorter" and the changelog says 2-30s. An estimate must therefore price the clip handed in, not a clip length requested, which is the same trap RBF-001 measured on Seedance.
duration.source: videoUri description in the spec, plus the Aleph 2.0 changelog entry

references.positions_note: Two mutually exclusive shapes: { uri, seconds } where seconds is an absolute timestamp 0-30 from the start, or { uri, at } where at is a fraction 0.0-1.0 of the input duration. THERE IS NO "first"/"last" KEYWORD — the aggregator described one. An optional `range` narrows the edit window, and all keyframes must either set a range or none may.
references.uri_note: HTTPS URL, Runway upload URI, or base64 data URI capped at 5MB.
references.source: Keyframe schema in the spec (anyOf of the seconds- and at-shaped variants)

pricing.unit: credits per second of INPUT video
pricing.source: Runway pricing guide: "28 credits per second (56 credit minimum per generation)"; one credit costs $0.01 in the developer portal

differences_from_aggregator.runway_says: videoUri, at the top level — there is no inputs object on this endpoint
promptText, and OPTIONAL — only videoUri and model are required
keyframes, pinned by an absolute `seconds` (0-30) or a fractional `at` (0.0-1.0). No first/last keyword exists.

differences_from_aggregator.aggregator_said: a 2-30s window presented as a request constraint
differences_from_aggregator.runway_says: no duration field on this variant at all; 30s is a bound on the SOURCE video

a base64 data URI is capped at 5MB for both videoUri and a keyframe uri — far below this engine's ~112MB upload path, so a source clip CANNOT travel inline and must be hosted (lib/frame-handles.js) or uploaded to Runway first
ratio is DEPRECATED on this endpoint; targetAspectRatio supersedes it with an eight-value enum
all four exist; outputFormat includes prores and png_sequence, which matters for a finishing pass

differences_note: SEVEN differences, and three of them would have produced a broken adapter: the video field is videoUri and not inputs.video, references are keyframes pinned by time rather than frameImages pinned to first/last, and a 5MB data-URI cap means a source clip cannot be sent inline at all. The credit rate and the 1000-character prompt cap were the two things the aggregator got right.
